output.brief:
The rise in cancellations is mostly not a pricing problem. It comes from the Quillbook accounting connector. Quillbook retired its old invoice interface on 30 March, and since then the connector has silently dropped or doubled invoices. 1,212 of 1,900 Quillbook accounts were hit, and 34% of those have cancelled, against 8% of the unaffected ones. Churn among Quillbook accounts is about 6%, whether they are repriced or price-locked, so price has no visible effect there. Accounts with no connector, which are most of the base, barely moved (1.9% against 1.8%), including the larger ones. The seat-size pattern in the finance analysis was confounded, because Quillbook accounts have more seats. I'm fairly confident, around 80–85%.

What to do:
- Make the Quillbook fix (move to the v3 interface, 3–4 weeks) the top engineering priority.
- Contact all Quillbook accounts, including those that cancelled, to correct their invoices.
- Make the connector's WARN-level failures visible on the health panel.
- Keep the duplicate-invoice hold. Switching it off would put duplicate invoices into customers' books.
- Don't roll back the price.
- Don't start the Tallymarsh rebuild yet. First review its log, since the signal there is tiny.
